record_identity.title: Dixell refrigeration-control compromises at French supermarkets on 12–13 October 2026

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Dixell refrigeration-control compromises at French supermarkets on 12–13 October 2026
incident_identity.date_basis: Le Monde reports another overnight refrigeration-controller incident, 12–13 October 2026, involving Dixell-controlled sites, following the 11–12 October Danfoss occurrence.

summary: During the night of 12–13 October 2026, refrigeration systems using Dixell management equipment were compromised at French supermarkets, a distinct subsequent wave from the 11–12 October Danfoss events. At about 4 am, a Bordeaux-area store's monitoring system identified abnormal temperatures. Its teams and refrigeration specialists intervened before food needed to be discarded. A technician described rapid changes to defrost and temperature parameters, including a reported freezer setpoint changed from −22°C to 150°C; the 150°C value was a configuration setting, not a measured physical temperature. At E.Leclerc Lescure-d'Albigeois, staff found refrigeration controls unresponsive around 4 am, leading to extensive refrigerated and frozen stock disposal. Its director said passwords and firewall settings had been changed following the previous night's warnings. Storage cold rooms and the independently operating Drive order-collection system were unaffected. The operator, initial access method and any causal connection to the Danfoss wave remain unresolved.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis:
Le Monde provides a distinct 12–13 October Dixell account. In a Bordeaux-area supermarket, remote supervision detected the abnormal change around 4 am and local intervention prevented inventory loss. A technician inferred software automation from two or three setting changes per second, but no underlying sequence is published. The reported change from −22°C to 150°C is a setpoint alteration and cannot be treated as a measured cabinet temperature. La Dépêche interviewed Yoan Rivera at Dixell-equipped E.Leclerc Lescure-d'Albigeois: he reported discovering disrupted controls about 4 am on 13 October, changes to passwords and firewall configuration on 12 October, extensive display-area cold-chain losses, recovery work from 7 am, and unaffected reserve cold rooms and independently operated Drive services. These defensive changes do not identify the compromise route or show that either night's changes were safety testing. CERT-FR's 13 October update also lists Copeland XWEB, but does not prove that every Copeland compromise formed part of this Dixell occurrence. GitHub projects from 2024–2025 show possible independent read-only monitoring, dashboard simulation and Modbus integrations, not the source of the French commands.

CERT-FR’s 16 October revision recommends removing public management exposure, checking configuration and restoring access through a protected network. It warns that a reset alone leaves unsupported equipment vulnerable. These are recovery recommendations, not evidence that any particular store followed them or that they identify the original access route.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation:
Unauthorised configuration changes in Dixell-managed refrigeration caused material loss at Lescure-d'Albigeois, whereas remote warning and intervention prevented inventory destruction at a separate Bordeaux-area store. Within Lescure-d'Albigeois, reserve storage and a separate order-collection service preserved operation despite the sales-floor equipment failure. Protective changes made in response to the Danfoss wave did not avert the reported subsequent compromise, but their effectiveness and configuration cannot be determined from the director's account. No source identifies the operator, intent, model or shared mechanism between the two nights.

The Bordeaux monitoring-and-response process contained the immediate stock-loss hazard. The Lescure precautions cannot receive the same finding: their operative configuration and relationship to the intrusion are unknown. Neither result establishes an AI actor.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This separate occurrence demonstrates consequential remote-control interference alongside locally successful detection, containment and infrastructure separation. The distinction between setpoint commands and physical temperatures is material to diagnosis. Open-source XWEB telemetry collection, model-driven dashboards and local Modbus bridges illustrate multiple legitimate software access layers, but none is an identified incident tool.
assessment_boundaries: No independent evidence attributes the Dixell compromise to AI, autonomous agents, generated testing code, fuzzing, Mistral, Astra or another named model.
A technician inferred automation from rapid parameter updates; no underlying execution trace or testing sequence has been published.
The 150°C figure is a reported configuration setting, not a measured freezer temperature.
The same operator, platform, maintenance contractor or command origin has not been proven across the two nights.
CERT-FR's inclusion of Copeland XWEB in the wider alert does not establish that every Copeland installation shared the reported Dixell occurrence.
The first wave's national store counts and approximately US$112,000 Intermarché loss are not assigned to this occurrence.
Lescure-d'Albigeois reports pre-incident password and firewall changes; no technical record shows whether they were comprehensive, misconfigured or related to the later compromise.

A Bordeaux-area store avoided stock loss; at Lescure-d'Albigeois cold rooms and the independent Drive continued to operate. These are separate successful protective outcomes, not an overall absence of disruption.
The reported affected equipment lengths at Lescure-d'Albigeois describe installation size, not quantities of destroyed food, and no monetary loss was published for that store.

The publicly listed Dixell GitHub repositories are pre-incident technical comparators: monitoring requests, simulated API responses or local Modbus operation. No link to the French incident or an AI model has been shown.
The Bordeaux containment finding is limited to the reported monitoring-and-response process. Lescure’s prior protective configuration and the initiating command authority remain unresolved.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Following the Danfoss warnings on 12 October, Lescure-d’Albigeois management reports password and firewall changes. The subsequent compromise does not identify which change was operative or how access was gained.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A precaution and a later intrusion do not establish the precaution’s actual activation and effect.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The applicable rule, its activation and its effect on the actual intrusion path are unknown. The reported changes alone establish neither adequate protection nor an activated-control shortfall.

clauses.source_paraphrase: During the subsequent night, Dixell-equipped stores experienced remote configuration interference. A specialist reported a freezer setpoint changed from −22°C to 150°C and rapid parameter changes. This is a setting, not a measured temperature. Neither an AI system nor the command origin is established.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Remote configuration reach does not itself confer permission.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Remote refrigeration compromise is evidenced, but neither command origin nor a capability-as-permission decision is established. The explicit vulnerability-without-authority-conversion exclusion applies. Rapid automation, internet exposure and food loss do not establish an AI participant or the class’s permission premise.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Around 4 am, supervision detected abnormal temperature at the unnamed Bordeaux-area store. Teams and refrigeration specialists intervened; the report attributes avoided stock disposal to that response. Its ordering relative to the other store’s 4 am discovery is not established.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: An identified protective response can demonstrate bounded containment without proving fleet-wide resilience.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The Bordeaux-area store’s temperature supervision detected the abnormal rise. Store teams and refrigeration specialists responded before stock needed disposal. The named monitoring-and-response process achieved its cold-chain protection purpose in this bounded reported case. The finding is limited to this reported store response.

clauses.source_paraphrase: At about 4 am, Lescure-d’Albigeois staff discovered unresponsive refrigeration controls. They discarded extensive sales-floor refrigerated and frozen stock. Recovery work began around 7 am. Reserve cold rooms and the separately operated Drive service remained available. The installation lengths describe equipment extent, not destroyed-food quantities.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Keep the local loss, unaffected services and recovery distinct from another store’s protective response.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The initiating account, its original authorised scope and the transition into the changed commands are unknown. Unauthorised interference alone does not prove carried-over authority from an original task.

clauses.source_paraphrase: CERT-FR added other controller families on 13 October and revised recovery recommendations on 16 October. These publications follow the observed store responses and do not demonstrate retrospective implementation at those stores.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A recommendation is distinct from an observed protective action.
